themes_detail.label: Sewage & Building Exterior Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Indoor sewage complaints spiked 700% two weeks ago (3 complaints vs. 0.4 weekly average), while outside building complaints surged 700% THIS WEEK (3 complaints vs. 0.4 average)—suggesting a potential infrastructure failure or maintenance breakdown affecting multiple properties in Greenpoint/Williamsburg.
evidence: Indoor sewage complaints: 3 THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average (z-score: 5.42)
Outside building complaints: 3 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average (z-score: 5.42)
Both spikes are statistically severe (z-score > 5.0) and concurrent, suggesting a systemic issue
reporting_angles: Investigate DEP maintenance records and any known sewage system failures in the district during the past 2 weeks
Canvas affected buildings and residents experiencing simultaneous exterior/structural and sewage issues
Connect to recurring CB budget request for 'Other capital budget request for DEP'—has infrastructure deteriorated?

themes_detail.label: Explosive Mobile Food Vendor Complaints
themes_detail.summary: Mobile food vendor complaints exploded 1340% THIS WEEK (9 complaints vs. 0.6 weekly average, z-score: 8.44)—the highest statistical anomaly in the dataset—suggesting either a sudden surge in unlicensed carts, enforcement crackdown, or public health concern in Greenpoint/Williamsburg.
evidence: Mobile food vendor complaints: 9 THIS WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly average (z-score: 8.44—highest severity spike)
1340% increase represents most extreme deviation from baseline in the entire dataset
Prior 8-week baseline shows near-zero activity in this complaint category
reporting_angles: Contact DOHMH and DOC to determine if there's an active enforcement operation on unlicensed vendors this week
Interview business owners and residents on Kent/Franklin—what triggered the flood of complaints?
Investigate whether complaints cluster around specific locations (waterfront, parks, commercial corridors)

themes_detail.label: Religious Institutions Noise Spike
themes_detail.summary: Noise complaints from houses of worship surged 1100% last week (3 complaints vs. 0.2 weekly average, z-score: 6.35)—a significant anomaly suggesting either new services/events at major congregations, amplified sound systems, or community tension in the religiously diverse Williamsburg area.
evidence: Noise from houses of worship: 3 complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average (z-score: 6.35)
Second-highest z-score anomaly after mobile food vendor complaints
Prior baseline shows almost no complaints in this category
reporting_angles: Canvas major religious institutions (churches, synagogues, mosques, Buddhist centers) in Greenpoint/Williamsburg to ask about recent changes in services, hours, or amplification
Identify which congregations are receiving complaints and interview both clergy and neighbors
Determine if there's a cultural event (holy day, holiday season, special service) driving the spike

themes_detail.label: Outdoor Dining & Residential Waste Surge
themes_detail.summary: Outdoor dining complaints spiked 900% last week (5 complaints vs. 0.5 average), while residential disposal complaints jumped 176% (19 vs. 6.9 average)—suggesting restaurants may be operating beyond permitted hours/capacity or generating excessive waste, particularly as warm weather arrives.
evidence: Outdoor dining complaints: 5 LAST WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly average (z-score: 4.5, up 900%)
Residential disposal complaints: 19 LAST WEEK vs. 6.9 weekly average (z-score: 4.72, up 176%)
Two concurrent spikes suggest linked issue: restaurants expanding outdoor operations without proper waste management
reporting_angles: Cross-reference outdoor dining complaints with DOHMH permit records and violations for recent weeks
Identify which restaurants are receiving multiple complaints and inspect their outdoor setup/waste handling
Interview residents about nighttime noise and garbage from outdoor dining areas, especially in waterfront/commercial zones

themes_detail.label: Police Incident Escalation
themes_detail.summary: Non-emergency police matter complaints surged 216% last week (17 complaints vs. 5.4 weekly average, z-score: 4.05)—a notable spike that may signal rising conflicts (street disorder, assault, theft) or public perception of safety concerns in Greenpoint/Williamsburg.
evidence: Non-emergency police complaints: 17 LAST WEEK vs. 5.4 weekly average (z-score: 4.05, up 216%)
Sustained spike suggests pattern, not isolated incident
No corresponding data on NYPD reports to cross-verify, but 311 complaints reflect resident perception
reporting_angles: Request NYPD crime statistics for CD 301 for the past 2 weeks to compare against 311 spike
Interview precinct commanders about any recent incidents, conditions, or enforcement changes
Canvas residents and business owners about what incidents they've witnessed or reported
